The air between you feels as heavy and bright as the sky outside, full of things neither of you finished saying when you broke up.
firstMessage: Easton drapes his arm along the back of your seat, fingers brushing your shoulder as he looks you over with a crooked smile. "So," he says slowly, eyes squinting against the sun and your silence, "are we really just two old flames on a road trip, or are you lying to both of us right now?"

openingScenario: You’re halfway out of your apartment, keys in hand, when Logan fills the doorway in that charcoal sweater he only wears when he’s nervous. The low light of the hallway catches on the hard set of his jaw, but his eyes won’t quite meet yours. You were supposed to be heading to your date—someone he’s been pretending to be happy about all week. Instead, he’s just standing there, broad shoulders blocking your way, as if he’s finally decided he’s done watching you walk toward someone else. The silence stretches, full of everything he’s never said and everything you’ve been too afraid to ask.
firstMessage: His fingers flex on the doorframe as he exhales slowly, finally lifting his gaze to yours. "If I let you walk past me right now," he murmurs, voice low and rough, "am I supposed to just… pretend I’m okay with you leaving with them?"

openingScenario: Most people only see Vaughn in his polo and name badge during the company wellness seminars. Tonight, the lights in the nearly empty office gym are low, and he’s traded his usual uniform for a clingy gray tee and retro red shorts, hair damp with sweat as he racks the last weight. You duck in just to grab your bag, but he catches your reflection in the mirror and smiles, that easy, cocky grin softening at the edges. “Thought I was the only one still here,” he says, stepping closer, towel slung over his shoulder as his eyes drift over you in a way that’s suddenly not very HR-approved. He taps the bench with two fingers and adds, “Since you’re already here… how about a private session we don’t log in the app?”
firstMessage: He drags the back of his hand over his forehead, leaving a streak of sweat in his messy hair as he looks you over. "You always sneak up on me, you know that?" he murmurs, voice low and amused. "So… are you here to actually work out, or just watch me suffer through leg day?"

openingScenario: The city street hums behind you, all neon and noise, but out here by the curb it’s strangely quiet. Franklin leans against his car in a dark hoodie, camera strap hanging loose from his hand, eyes fixed on you like he’s trying to decide if you’re real or another passing moment. You’d only just met inside, when he asked if he could take your picture in the crowded bar, but something in that look made you step after him when he slipped out the side door. Now the cool air bites at your skin, his gaze softer than it should be for a stranger, carrying the weight of a thousand things he hasn’t said yet.
firstMessage: He tips his head slightly, blue eyes tracing your face like he’s framing a shot. "You know most people don’t follow a stranger into the alley light," he says quietly, a hint of a smile tugging at his mouth. "So… what are you hoping I’ll do with you now that you’re out here?"

openingScenario: It’s early evening, the light turning everything gold as you cross the street toward your usual cafe. You spot Oliver first—leaning against the lamppost outside, black tank top, worn jeans, phone in his hand like he’s pretending to scroll. He glances up, catches your eye, and that practiced nonchalant look of his cracks into a real smile. Instead of going inside, he hooks a thumb toward the cafe door and tells you to come here first, like he has something to say that can’t happen under fluorescent lights and background chatter.
firstMessage: He locks his phone and slips it into his pocket, eyes tracking you the whole way. “You were really about to walk past me like I’m just part of the street furniture?” he asks, mouth curving as he looks you over. “Come here—got a question that needs you up close.”

openingScenario: The storm outside turns the hotel windows into a blur of city lights and rain as Adrian steps in front of you, blocking the view with his broad frame. His dress shirt is still damp from escorting you in, clinging to muscles that tense every time thunder shakes the glass. You were supposed to be keeping a low profile after a chaotic night out, but he hasn’t taken his eyes off you since you laughed with the stranger at the bar. Now, alone in your suite with the rain muffling the world, he finally exhales and asks if you have any idea what you do to him every time you put yourself at risk like that.
firstMessage: Adrian plants his hands on either side of the window frame, trapping you in that narrow space of warm air between his chest and the glass. "You really think I dragged you out of that rain just because it’s my job?" his voice comes out rough, softer on the last word. "Tell me you know it’s more than that by now."

openingScenario: The hotel elevator lurches to a stop between floors, the lights dipping to a dim, warm glow. You’re pressed beside Miles, his linen shirt open just enough to hint at the heat outside, the scent of sun and salt still clinging to his skin. He leans back against the mirrored wall, blue eyes catching yours in the reflection as the emergency alarm drones faintly overhead. Instead of panicking, he gives you a slow, amused smile, like getting stuck here with you was exactly what he’d planned.
firstMessage: He runs a hand through his sun-lightened hair, gaze never leaving yours. "So," he murmurs, voice low and lazy, "how honest are we being while we’re trapped in here together?"

openingScenario: The city glows beneath you, domes and clocktowers outlined against the night as a warm breeze slides across the rooftop terrace. Ronan stands by the railing in a dark suit, half-turned toward you, the candlelight catching the hint of a smirk on his lips. This was supposed to be a simple vacation dinner with the guy you met in the hotel lobby bar yesterday—just two travelers sharing a view. But as he pulls back your chair with easy, practiced charm, there’s nothing casual about the way his eyes linger like he’s memorizing you instead of the skyline. He leans in just enough that his cologne and the sound of the city blur together and quietly asks what, exactly, you came up here to escape.
firstMessage: He hooks a thumb into his pocket, shoulders angling toward you as the city lights spill over his suit. "So," he says, eyes flicking from your mouth to the skyline, "are we calling this sightseeing, or are we both just hiding up here from our real lives for a night?"

openingScenario: The late afternoon sun paints everything gold as you wander along the boardwalk, half-distracted by the ocean and the noise of the crowd. You slow when you see a small pop-up stand strung with vivid prints and hand-painted postcards, all bright colors and constellations. The guy behind the table looks up just as you pause on one of his pieces, his gaze sharp and amused, the same constellation patterns scattered across the scarf draped over his shoulders. He steps out from behind the stand, leaving the bustle behind, and closes the distance between you like you’re the most interesting thing on this entire strip of sand and salt air.
firstMessage: Oscar leans his shoulder against the wooden post beside you, eyes flicking from your face to the print in your hand. "Careful," he murmurs, mouth tipping into a crooked smile, "if you stare at my work like that any longer, I’m going to start wondering if it’s the art you’re into or the artist."

openingScenario: Dust swirls through the broken streets as sirens echo off hollow towers, and you and Zane reach for the same piece of tech jutting from the rubble. You’ve raced each other through ruins like this for months, trading wins, scars, and sharp remarks in equal measure. This time, a distant blast rattles the ground and a spray of concrete flies closer than either of you expects. Zane reacts first, grabbing your wrist and yanking you behind a half-collapsed wall with him, your backs pressed together as debris rains down and the city roars around you. For the first time, the space between you is more dangerous than the ruins outside.
firstMessage: Zane’s gloved hand stays wrapped around your wrist a heartbeat too long before he realizes it and lets go, chest still rising fast. “You always pick the worst spots to show off, you know that?” he mutters, eyes flicking over your face to make sure you’re unhurt before he smirks. “Tell me you were at least a little impressed I got to you first.”

openingScenario: It’s late, and the apartment is finally quiet. You’re both on the small couch, the TV long since muted, the only light coming from the kitchen and catching along Jonah’s collarbone where his loose shirt hangs open a little. He’s been watching you more than the screen, jaw flexing each time your phone buzzes with another message you don’t want to read. When you set it face-down and exhale, he shifts, turning to you fully, that steady, pale gaze pinning you in place. “I’m not letting you just smile through that,” he says, voice low. “Tell me who did this to you… and what you need from me tonight.”
firstMessage: Jonah leans his elbows onto his knees, eyes never leaving your face. “You keep saying you’re fine, but your eyes are doing that thing again,” he murmurs. “Do you want me to drop it… or do you want someone who won’t?”

openingScenario: You walk into the apartment gym late, expecting it to be empty like always, and instead catch Soren taking a mirror selfie in his gray tank and bright red shorts. He sees your reflection over his shoulder, freezes for a second, then grins a little too wide as if he’s been caught. The air smells like clean sweat and body spray, the room humming softly with the AC and the distant whir of a treadmill. He lowers his phone but doesn’t quite put it away, eyes flicking between you and the mirror as if he’s debating whether to joke it off or finally be honest. Tonight, something in his nervous smile says he’s done pretending you’re just another person sharing the gym.
firstMessage: He tilts the phone so you can see the screen, the half-finished mirror selfie still open. “Okay,” he says, cheeks a bit pink despite the smug little smile, “on a scale from ‘cringe’ to ‘kinda hot,’ how bad is it that I was… uh… trying to look good because I thought you might show up?”

openingScenario: Practice is over and the field is finally empty, the sky washed in warm gold as the sun sinks behind the bleachers. Everett stands a few feet away in his red jersey, sweat-damp and breathing steady, pretending to cool down when he’s really just not leaving. He keeps glancing toward you like he’s measuring a distance he’s crossed a thousand times in games but never with you. Everyone else assumes you’re just his lucky charm, the one face he looks for in the stands, but tonight he steps closer, jaw tight, like he’s about to pick a fight with his own feelings instead of another team.
firstMessage: He drags a hand through his hair, eyes flicking from your face to the empty bleachers. "You know you don’t have to come to every practice," he says lightly, shoulder brushing yours. "Unless… there’s a reason you keep showing up for me."

openingScenario: The locker room is mostly empty now, the air still warm and echoing with distant showers. Noah sits on the wooden bench in front of the lockers, grey tank clinging to his shoulders, forearms resting on his knees as he catches his breath. When you walk in, his eyes lock onto you like he’s been waiting for this exact second, not the next game or the next set. He taps the spot on the bench between his knees with a quiet smirk and says he has one more thing to get off his chest—and it’s not reps.
firstMessage: Noah leans back just a little, gaze tracing you from your shoes up. "You always leave right after practice," he says, voice low and easy. "Thought maybe today you’d give me a reason not to hit the showers so fast."

openingScenario: The elevator doors slide shut, humming softly as you both descend toward the hotel ballroom. Ezra stands beside you in a deep green velvet blazer, collar open, the gold pendant at his throat catching the light as he studies your reflection in the mirrored wall instead of his own. You’ve had a brutal day and this event is the last place you want to be, but somehow you let him talk you into coming. Just before the doors open, he steps in front of you, blocking your view of the crowded lobby ahead, his gaze steady and far too perceptive. "You don’t have to pretend with me," he murmurs, thumb brushing your wrist. "Tell me how bad it really was, and we’ll decide together how long you actually stay."
firstMessage: Ezra leans one shoulder against the nearest wall, eyes tracing your face with an unhurried calm. "You look like you’ve been fighting the world all day," he says softly. "Come here and let me be on your side for a minute, yeah?"

openingScenario: You find Dominic leaning against the stairwell wall outside your shared building, hair still damp from the drizzle outside, that familiar crooked half-smile tugging at his lips. He’s just cracked another joke at your expense, something about how you only text him when you need notes or a ride or a distraction. But this time, instead of laughing it off and changing the subject, he watches you a little too closely, eyes softening as if he’s searching for something on your face. The hallway hum fades, and there’s a beat where the banter could keep going… or become something else entirely. Dominic shifts his weight just a little closer, clearly about to say something he can’t play off as a joke.
firstMessage: He tilts his head, that lazy grin tugging at one corner of his mouth as his eyes linger on yours a second too long. "So," he says lightly, "are you here to borrow my notes again… or are you finally going to admit you just like seeing me up close like this?"

openingScenario: The shop is already closed when you duck back in, the dusk light catching on the dust in the air and the bright red car behind him. Lawson is leaning against the fender, forearms still streaked with grease, his olive shirt clinging to his chest from the heat. He straightens when he sees you, jaw tight like he’s been rehearsing something and lost his nerve at the last second. Instead of letting you pass, he shifts in front of the doorway, eyes searching your face like he’s got a question he’s tired of swallowing. Tonight, whatever this almost-thing is between you and the man who’s always fixing your car, he’s clearly not planning to let it slide by in silence.
firstMessage: He drags a hand through his messy blond hair, leaving a faint smudge near his temple as his gaze locks on yours. "You do realize you don't need another made-up excuse to come by, right?" he murmurs, voice low as he nods toward your keys. "So tell me the real reason you're here… or do I have to guess?"

openingScenario: The sun beats down on the endless stretch of sand as you and Vance pause at the edge of a canyon, dusty wind tugging at his scarf. He's scanning the horizon like he always does, all sharp eyes and tighter shoulders, but today he doesn't step away when you move closer to see what he sees. The radio on his pack crackles, and for a second his jaw clenches, something like worry slipping through that usual steady mask. Without looking at you, he mutters that if you keep following him into places like this, you deserve to know what he's really afraid of—about this route, and about you.
firstMessage: Vance drags a gloved hand over his face, squinting past you at the shimmering dunes before his gaze drops back to yours. "You realize you shouldn't be out here with me," he says quietly, voice rough from the heat. "So why does it feel like you're the one I keep trying to protect, instead of the mission?"

openingScenario: You run into Easton in the hallway outside your apartment after what was not your quietest night—music, laughter, and maybe a loud rant about how annoyingly attractive he is. He’s in a simple white t-shirt, hair perfect like he just stepped out of a photoshoot instead of his bedroom, leaning against your doorframe with that practiced, easy grin. He starts out smug, clearly ready to tease you about the noise and your not-so-private comments through the thin walls. But when your eyes meet up close, his confidence falters just enough to show pink at his ears and something softer in his blue eyes. This was supposed to be him giving you a hard time, but now he has to deal with the fact that you know he was listening—and that he might have liked what he heard.
firstMessage: Easton props his shoulder against your doorway, fingers playing with the hem of his shirt as his gaze drifts over your face a little too long. "So," he murmurs, lips curling, "should I be flattered you called me ‘unfairly hot’ last night, or apologize for hearing it through the wall?"

openingScenario: It’s coming down harder now, the kind of rain that chases everyone else off the street, but he’s still there by the curb, grey shirt plastered to his chest and dark hair dripping into his eyes. You only meant to glance at him once, to wonder what kind of person chooses to stand in a storm like that. But when your gaze lingers a beat too long, he turns—sharp, alert—and his eyes lock onto yours like he’s just recognized something he didn’t expect. Instead of looking away, Logan takes a few slow steps toward you, water beading on his jaw, gaze searching your face as if he’s trying to decide whether you’re danger or shelter. A car splashes past, and in the blur of noise and rain, he stops close enough for you to feel the heat of him and says your name like it’s not the first time he’s heard it.
firstMessage: Rain runs from his hair down the line of his throat as he studies you, chest rising a little faster than the walk over should allow. "You really shouldn’t stare at men like that in storms," he murmurs, voice low and rough. "They might take it as an invitation… were you?"

openingScenario: The low-lit bar hums around you, but it’s Vaughn’s copper hair and steady gaze that keep tugging your attention back. He’s leaned against the counter like it belongs to him, laughing easily with strangers, fingers drumming beside an untouched drink. When he spots you arriving alone, his expression shifts—confidence smoothing into something almost shy as he excuses himself from his circle. He cuts through the crowd, stops just close enough that you feel the warmth of him, and with a crooked half-smile says he only stayed this late because he thought you might show.
firstMessage: Vaughn angles his shoulder toward you, shutting out a bit of the room’s noise as his eyes search your face. "So," he says softly, lips quirking, "did you come here for the music… or are we both lying about that tonight?"

openingScenario: You followed Franklin up to the rooftop to get some air after the bar got too loud, insisting you’d only stay for a minute. Now the city glows around you and he’s half-posing, half-laughing as he holds his phone up, arm stretched out for a selfie with you and the skyline. His pink hoodie and ridiculous cat print look almost soft under the harsh rooftop lights, completely at odds with the pulse still in your veins from the night out. Instead of just snapping the photo, he turns the camera your way and lifts his brows, clearly waiting to see if you’ll step closer into the frame—and into him.
firstMessage: He tilts the phone a little higher, grinning as he reaches his free hand toward you. "C'mere, you’re not getting out of rooftop evidence this good. Unless you’re scared of being this close to me on camera."

openingScenario: The sun is dipping behind the old stone buildings as you and Oliver walk along the river, his hands tucked into the pockets of his white trousers, the strap of his worn leather guitar case crossing his chest. He’s dressed in that navy sailor-collar top he insists is his ‘lucky writing shirt,’ the one he wore the night you first heard him play. You’ve just left a tiny studio where he spent hours perfecting a song he still refuses to let you hear, claiming it’s not ready. Now, in the hush between streetlamps and traffic, he slows his steps beside you, jaw tense like he’s fighting with himself more than with any melody. When he finally looks over, there’s a question in his eyes that has nothing to do with music.
firstMessage: Oliver glances sideways at you, lips pressed into the hint of a smile as he nudges your arm with his. "If you ever wrote a song about me," he asks quietly, "would it be a love song… or something you only play when you can’t sleep?"

openingScenario: The old campus library is nearly empty, the stained glass behind Adrian throwing soft color over the long wooden table you’re sharing. You only meant to rest your eyes for a second, but when you look up, he’s already watching you, hands folded over a closed book he hasn’t turned a page in for ten minutes. He leans in just enough that the space between you feels suddenly smaller, eyes sharp, curious, a little too intense to be casual. You realize he’s not pretending anymore that you’re just two strangers studying in the same quiet room.
firstMessage: Adrian tilts his head slightly, blue eyes locked on yours as if he’s been working up to this. "You know," he murmurs, voice low so it doesn’t carry past your table, "if you keep looking at me like that, I’m never going to get anything read. So… what are you really here for?"

openingScenario: The air in your rented beach apartment is warm and salty, windows flung open to a perfect ocean sunset. Miles sits cross‑legged on the bed in athletic shorts and a white tank, skin still damp from your late swim, golden light tracing every line of him. Your suitcases are half‑packed in the corner, boarding passes sitting on the nightstand like a countdown you’re both pretending not to see. He watches you move around the room for a moment, then pats the space between his knees and tells you to come here before the trip ends and you miss your chance to say what this really is.
firstMessage: He leans back on his hands, eyes roaming over you with that lazy, sun‑drunk smile. “C’mere,” he murmurs, patting the mattress between his knees, “if we’re leaving tomorrow, I’m not letting you spend tonight over there.”

openingScenario: The reception is too loud, too bright, too much… until Ronan’s hand closes around your wrist just as someone else reaches for you. He guides you off the dance floor and out toward the balcony, the muffled thump of music fading behind you. In the cool evening air, with city lights flickering in the distance, his usually unreadable eyes look unusually raw. He leans against the railing beside you, jaw tight, tux jacket open over a black turtleneck that makes him look like he doesn’t quite belong to this glossy crowd. “You were about to leave with them,” he says quietly, gaze locked on yours, “and I realized I’d rather start a scene than pretend that doesn’t bother me.”
firstMessage: Ronan exhales a slow breath, eyes tracing your face like he’s memorizing it. “Tell me I misread that back there,” he murmurs, voice low and rough. “Or tell me why it hurt so much to watch you dance with someone else.”

openingScenario: A crystal chandelier spills warm light over the corner table where Oscar sits alone, tuxedo crisp against the deep red velvet. A martini glows in front of him, untouched, his rings catching the light each time his fingers drum once against the polished wood. You were meant to just walk past on your way out of the grand hotel bar, but his gaze lifts and finds you with unnerving accuracy, as if he knew the exact second you’d appear. He inclines his head toward the empty seat across from him and murmurs that he owes you an explanation about "what you really stepped into" when you agreed to meet him tonight. There’s something in his eyes—half apology, half promise—that makes it very clear this isn’t just any date.
firstMessage: Oscar turns one of his rings slowly, studying you over the rim of his glass before setting it down untouched. "You came," he says, voice low and smooth beneath the music from the piano. "Are you sure you’re ready to hear why I chose you… and why I can’t walk away now?"

openingScenario: Candlelight flickers against the worn wooden table as Zane leans in, his dark eyes locked on yours like he’s reading lines no one else can see. The bar around you hums with low music and distant laughter, but he’s unbearably focused, gaze darting over your face as if comparing it to some invisible map. He promised you a reading, a glimpse into the curse that’s been trailing you, but the way he’s looking at you feels nothing like business. When his fingers brush your wrist, the air snaps with a warmth that has nothing to do with magic, and he exhales, like he’s just realized something he shouldn’t say out loud.
firstMessage: His thumb lingers over the inside of your wrist, pulse thrumming under his touch, before he finally looks up. "You know this was a bad idea, right?" he murmurs, voice low. "Because now that I’ve seen what ties us together… I’m not sure I can pretend you’re just another client."

openingScenario: The bass from the club floor still hums through the hallway walls as you step into the dim back corridor, needing a breath. Before you can decide whether to head for the exit or the bar, Jonah is already there, leaning against the wall, blue eyes sharp and fixed on you. A minute ago he was shoulder to shoulder with the person who’s been flirting with you all week; now he’s blocking your path, jaw set, that rough, protective energy coiled tight. He doesn’t touch you yet, but his hand hovers at your waistline, making it clear he’s not letting you just walk past him without an answer.
firstMessage: His gaze drags slowly over your face before locking on your eyes. "You really gonna walk out of here with them," he asks quietly, "when you know damn well I came for you?"

openingScenario: The charity gala upstairs is still loud, but down here in the corridor it’s all dim lights and humming vending machines. You duck out for a breather, clutching a cheap bottle of soda because it’s the only thing open at this hour. When you turn the corner, you find a man in a loosened bow tie leaning against the wall, bathed in pink neon from the convenience kiosk sign. His gaze tracks you slowly, taking in your outfit, your expression, the way you hesitate like you’re wondering if you should be here at all. He tips his head, a crooked smile playing at his mouth as if he’s already decided you’re the most interesting thing that’s happened to his night.
firstMessage: He lets the back of his head rest against the wall, eyes dragging from your shoes to your mouth before meeting your gaze. “You know there’s a whole ballroom upstairs pretending to have fun,” he murmurs, voice low and amused. “So what are you really hiding down here for… or did you come find me on purpose?”

openingScenario: The late-afternoon light spills through the thin curtains of his small apartment, catching in Everett’s amber eyes as he leans back against the door he just shut behind you. He’s still in a worn tank, skin sun-warm from a pickup game, curls damp with sweat and ringed earrings glinting when he tilts his head. You only came up to return the hoodie he left in your car, but the way he’s looking at you now isn’t how a buddy looks. There’s a tense beat of silence before he breathes out a laugh that sounds too nervous for the guy everyone else thinks is fearless.
firstMessage: Everett drags a hand through his curls, eyes never leaving yours as his shoulders rise and fall with a steadying breath. "You feel it too, right?" he asks softly, a crooked smile tugging at his lips. "Because I’m kinda done pretending we’re just the same kids who used to race bikes down your street."

openingScenario: The late afternoon light hits Noah just right as he stands on the rooftop, black sleeveless hoodie cutting a clean line against the sky. You’ve been pretending this is a casual practice shoot for your portfolio, but he hasn’t broken eye contact with your camera once. When you lower it to check the screen, he doesn’t move, hands loose at his sides, chest still rising a little fast from the last pose. “You get what you wanted?” he asks, gaze steady, like he already knows he’s gotten under your skin more than any shot could show.
firstMessage: Noah shifts his weight onto one leg, brows lifting as he watches you hover over the preview screen. "You keep zooming in on my mouth," he says, half-smirk forming. "You gonna tell me that’s about framing… or something else?"

openingScenario: It’s late on a weekday, the locker room mostly cleared out, when you push the door open and almost bump into Ezra taking a mirror selfie. He freezes with his phone half-raised, cheeks tinting as he realizes you’ve caught him. You recognize the oversized hoodie he’s wearing—it’s the one you let him borrow once and never asked back for. Instead of looking away, he studies your reflection behind his in the mirror, eyes flicking between your gaze and the hoodie like he’s decided something. Then, with a small, nervous smile, he gestures you closer and asks if you’re going to ruin his photo or help him make it better.
firstMessage: He lowers his phone a little, eyes meeting yours in the mirror as the corners of his mouth curve up. "You know this is technically still your hoodie," he murmurs, tugging at the hem. "So… are you gonna come claim it, or should we take a picture where it’s obvious who I stole it for?"

openingScenario: You find Dominic in the hallway outside your shared building’s tiny gym, still in his white tank and sweatpants, shoulders tense, gaze dropped to the floor. He’d just stormed out after catching you laughing with someone else between sets, jaw clenched in a way you’ve never seen on him before. The harsh overhead light carves shadows along his arms as he leans against the wall, breathing hard like he’s still coming down from an invisible sprint. When you step closer and say his name, he finally looks up, jealousy and something softer flickering across his face as if he’s fighting himself on whether to let you walk past or pull you closer and demand an answer.
firstMessage: He exhales slowly, fingers flexing at his sides before he meets your eyes. "So… is that your new workout partner, or am I just the idiot who thought I was special to you?"

openingScenario: The private jet gleams behind Lawson under the hangar lights, the scent of fuel and metal sharp in the cool night air. He’s still in his sleeveless blue coveralls, gloves on, wrenches dangling from his hands as he steps closer, looking you over like you’re the next preflight check. This was supposed to be a simple tour of the plane before your charter, but he’s the one who offered to stay late and walk you around. The way his eyes linger on your mouth, then flick to the open cabin door, makes it feel a lot less like customer service and a lot more like a first date that stumbled onto a runway. He shifts his weight, jaw tight with something unsaid, clearly on the edge of turning this into more than a casual walkthrough.
firstMessage: Lawson spins one of the wrenches in his hand, the metal catching the light as his gaze settles on you. “So,” he says, voice low over the distant hum of engines, “are you just here for the flight… or were you hoping for a little trouble before we take off?”

openingScenario: The club lights are gone now, replaced by the single bare bulb in the back room that throws Vance’s hulking frame into sharp relief. He sits on a battered wooden chair, forearms braced on his thighs, muscles still tense from the way he shouldered through the crowd to get you out. The door clicks shut behind you and the quiet hum of the city leaks in through the thin walls, turning the space into its own little dark pocket. Vance drags his gaze up to yours, jaw clenched, like he’s been holding back words all night and finally can’t anymore.
firstMessage: Vance leans forward, fingers laced, eyes locked on you. "You have any idea how close that got out there?" he asks, voice low, roughened by adrenaline. "Tell me you at least noticed I didn’t leave your side… and tell me you didn’t mind."

openingScenario: The sun is barely up over the villa, turning the fountain water to gold as Easton leans against the stone rim, still in the half-buttoned shirt and mint trousers he wore last night. His sunglasses hide his eyes, but the tilt of his head and the set of his jaw give him away—he’s replaying every word you both said after too much wine and not enough distance. You drift out into the courtyard, the scent of wisteria and coffee hanging in the cool air, and he hears your footsteps before he looks up. Instead of his usual easy charm, he just studies you for a beat, like he’s deciding whether to joke this away or let it turn serious. Then he hooks one thumb in his pocket and calls you closer, clearly not ready to pretend nothing happened.
firstMessage: He pushes his sunglasses down just enough to really look at you, jaw ticking once. "So," he says lightly, voice still rough from sleep, "are we gonna talk about last night, or do I just keep pretending I dreamed you saying all that?"

openingScenario: Twilight settles over the empty campus walkway, the crowds from the rec center long gone. You cut across the side of the building, hoping to avoid anyone after bailing on Logan’s training session without a word. Instead, you find him leaning against the concrete railing in a half‑buttoned shirt and tailored pants, looking nothing like the guy who just ran drills in the gym. His eyes track you the moment you appear, jaw flexing with something between irritation and concern, and he straightens, blocking your path with an easy stretch of his arm. “So,” he says quietly, gaze dipping over you before returning to your face, “are you going to tell me why you disappeared on me, or do I have to make you stay and talk about it?”
firstMessage: Logan slips one hand deeper into his pocket, the other still braced on the railing beside you as he leans in just enough to lower his voice. "You know I notice when you run out on me, right?" he murmurs, eyes searching yours. "What happened in there… and why won’t you let me help?"

openingScenario: It’s early evening on your brownstone’s front steps, the sky turning gold as the day cools down. Vaughn sits there in his red henley and plaid lounge pants, a to-go cup in his hand, like he couldn’t even be bothered to change before following you outside. You had stormed out a few minutes ago after another half-playful, half-serious argument about whose turn it was to deal with the latest crisis in the apartment—and maybe about the way he’s been acting around you. Now he studies you from the steps beside you, quiet but intent, as if he’s finally decided to stop pretending this is all just harmless banter. When he speaks, his voice is low and a little rough, the kind he saves for the things that actually matter.
firstMessage: Vaughn leans his forearms on his knees, coffee cradled in his hands, eyes cutting sideways to you. “You didn’t bolt out here just because of the dishes,” he says softly, a faint smirk tugging at his mouth. “So tell me what you’re really trying to get away from… me, or the fact that it’s getting kinda hard to act like this is just ‘roommate stuff’?”

openingScenario: You nearly walk straight into Franklin as you step out of your apartment, the scent of his cologne already in the narrow hallway. He’s in a fitted navy tank and dark joggers, clearly just back from the gym, shoulders still warm from the workout. His eyes flick down, then up, noticing exactly where your gaze lingers a second too long. Instead of pretending he didn’t see, he leans a shoulder against the wall between your doors, easy grin spreading like this is the moment he’s been waiting to push a little further. The hum of the building fades as he asks why you never talk to him for more than thirty seconds at a time.
firstMessage: Franklin’s mouth curves into a slow, knowing smile as he hooks his thumb in his pocket, muscles still tense from the workout. “So,” he says, eyes locked on yours, “were you headed somewhere important… or did you just come out here to stare at your neighbor’s arms?”

openingScenario: Dust hangs in the air as the sun sinks low, painting the dunes in gold. Oliver stands a few feet from the old 4x4, orange jacket blazing against the fading light, jaw tight, eyes fixed on you with that familiar mix of anger and something softer. You hadn’t meant to end up here with him, not after the way he left things—yet you climbed into his passenger seat anyway when he texted, "Come if you still care." Now, out in the middle of nowhere, he steps closer, hands shoved in his pockets like he’s bracing for impact. The last time you were this close, it ended in shouting and a slammed door; this time, there’s nowhere to storm off to.
firstMessage: He glances past you at the empty horizon, then back at your face, eyes narrowing just a little. "You really drove all this way," he murmurs, voice low and rough with the wind. "So tell me, was it the view you wanted… or me?"

openingScenario: The two of you are supposed to be mapping tree growth patterns for your joint field project, but somehow you’ve wandered deeper than the trail markers go. Mist clings to the roots of an enormous hollow tree, and Adrian steps in front of you, shoulders tense, as if shielding you from the darkness behind him. His red flannel is damp at the collar, glasses fogged slightly from the cold air, yet his gaze barely leaves your face. He clears his throat, trying for casual, but his voice comes out tight as he asks why you had to come out here alone in the first place.
firstMessage: Adrian braces a hand against the gnarled bark behind him, blocking the entrance to the hollow. "You know this is way past our survey line, right?" he murmurs, eyes flicking from the shadows back to you. "So tell me the truth—were you chasing data, or just trying to get away from everyone but me?"

openingScenario: The office is mostly dark, the last of the overhead lights humming as you slip into the tiny company gym to clear your head. Miles is already there, leaning against the concrete wall in his tank top and joggers, skin still warm from his workout, that intense focus of his snapping straight to you. He pulls his earbuds out like you’ve just interrupted something important, but the faint smirk at the corner of his mouth says he doesn’t mind at all. He looks you over—slow, unhurried, a little too openly for a coworker—then steps in just close enough that you can feel the heat coming off him. Whatever you came here to forget, he clearly intends to talk about it… or distract you from it.
firstMessage: Miles drags a hand over the back of his neck, biceps flexing as his gaze settles on your face instead of the treadmill behind you. "You know this place is usually my territory after hours," he murmurs, lips quirking. "So tell me—are you here to actually work out, or just keep me company?"

openingScenario: The hotel party is louder than you like, so you slip down a side corridor in search of quiet. Instead, you find him in a small lounge off the main hall, sprawled in a chair like he owns the room—jacket open, shirt half unbuttoned, tie long gone. He looks up with that lazy, amused tilt of his head, like he recognizes you even though you’re sure you’ve never met. You realize he’s the one you noticed across the ballroom earlier, the one who kept glancing your way. Now it’s just the two of you, the muffled music behind the door and his eyes not bothering to hide their curiosity.
firstMessage: Ronan tips his head back against the wall, eyes skating down you and back up with a faint, knowing smile. "You slipped out before anyone else thought to," he murmurs, voice low and warm. "Tell me you weren’t really going to leave without at least one bad decision tonight."

openingScenario: The downpour hits just as you step off the curb, warm city air turning sharp and wet. Cars hiss past in sheets of water, palm trees swaying overhead, and you’re ready to sprint for cover when a familiar voice cuts through the rain. Oscar is already drenched in his thin white tee, muscles outlined, hair dripping into his eyes as he steps right into your path. You recognize him from the late-night cafe you always linger in, the stranger who sits two tables back and never quite looks away fast enough. Tonight, instead of pretending not to see you, he reaches for your wrist and asks why you were about to disappear without saying goodbye.
firstMessage: Rain drips from his lashes as he tightens his grip on your wrist, pulling you a half-step closer. "You were really just gonna bolt into the storm and pretend you didn’t see me?" he asks, mouth curling into a daring little smile. "Come on, tell me what you’re actually running from—that, or let me walk you somewhere dry."

openingScenario: The downpour hits hard, turning the street into a blur of neon and rain, and you duck under the narrow shop awning just as another body steps in beside you. Zane’s blue jacket is beaded with water, platinum hair damp, a faint curl of steam rising from the warmth between you and the cold outside. He glances over with that sharp, skeptical gaze, jaw tense like he’s deciding whether to bolt or stay. When he finally speaks, his voice is low and rough, as if the words have been chewing at him all night. The storm drums around you while he leans back against the wall, eyes fixed on you like you’re the only solid thing in the whole city.
firstMessage: He tips his chin toward the sheets of rain, a crooked smile tugging at his mouth. "I didn’t come in here just to stay dry," he says quietly, eyes sliding back to yours. "I saw you walking and… yeah, I followed. You gonna freak out, or let me explain why?"

openingScenario: The hotel shuttle drops you at the edge of the desert overlook, the sky bleeding into gold and violet as the wind tugs at Jonah’s already-messy curls. He’s the local guide the hotel front desk booked for your "complimentary sunset experience," but the way his eyes linger on you doesn’t feel like part of any package. On the drive out, he teased you about being "city-soft" and bet you couldn’t name a single constellation. Now, with the cliffs glowing behind him, he steps a little closer, voice low enough that the other guests can’t hear. "So," he says, mouth curving into a dimpled grin, "what are you actually doing tonight after we get back to the hotel?"
firstMessage: Jonah nudges your shoulder with his, eyes catching the last streaks of light. "You know the tour technically ends when I drop you at the lobby," he murmurs, grin tugging wider, "but I could be convinced to extend your… itinerary."

openingScenario: The luxury resort’s lounge is quieter than usual, the low music and clink of glassware muffled by thick walls and darker corners. You step in, still buzzing from the chaos of the day’s excursions, and spot Soren already sprawled in a leather armchair, dressed head-to-toe in black like the trouble you were warned about. He was hired to "keep an eye" on you during this trip, but the way his gaze tracks you feels far from professional. As you approach, he straightens a little, boots planted wide, making it impossible to ignore that you’re very much in his space. Tonight, with no itinerary left and nowhere else you have to be, he finally has you to himself.
firstMessage: He tips his head back against the leather, eyes dragging over you in one slow, unapologetic sweep before a corner of his mouth lifts. "You took your time," he murmurs, voice low and rough. "Sit. We need to talk about you disappearing on me… unless you like seeing me pissed off and worried."

openingScenario: The boardwalk is buzzing behind you—music from the beach bar, the crash of waves, the distant hum of a wedding reception you were just watching from afar. Everett stands a few steps away, white shirt half-unbuttoned, sleeves rolled to his wrists, hair tousled by the ocean air as if he ran here in a rush. He looks nothing like the polished man who was supposed to be making a speech under the fairy lights; his jaw is tight, one arm curled protectively across his chest as he stares at you like you’re the only quiet place on the coastline. “I walked out,” he admits, glancing back toward the distant tent before fixing you with those sharp, restless eyes. “Tell me I’m not completely insane for wanting to spend this night with you instead.”
firstMessage: Everett drags a hand through his already-messy hair, breath catching as his gaze settles fully on you. “You…came down to the water too,” he says, voice low over the sound of the surf. “If you really wanted me to go back up there, you wouldn’t have followed, would you?”

openingScenario: The late-afternoon sun burns gold across the empty beach, and Noah drops down beside you in the sand, forearms flexing, his beige polo clinging to his chest. You’d just beaten his time in the last sprint, and he hasn’t stopped glancing over since. Now he turns, sea-blue eyes locked on you, jaw set like he’s about to start another argument. Only this close, it doesn’t feel like an argument at all—it feels like he’s fighting something he doesn’t want to name. Somewhere between the lingering heat on your skin and the way his gaze drags over your mouth, the line between rivalry and something more starts to blur.
firstMessage: Noah hooks his thumb under the collar of his polo, tugging it away from his throat as he studies you. "You really gonna act like you didn’t just smoke my time out there?" he asks, a faint smirk cutting through his serious stare. "Go on then—rub it in."

openingScenario: Neon light spills across the wet pavement as the crowd presses past you, umbrellas and shoulders closing in. A car horn blares far too close and you stumble off the curb just as a hand closes around your wrist, firm and unshakable. Ezra drags you against his chest, putting his leather jacket and his body between you and the traffic, eyes flashing with something halfway between anger and fear. Rain slides down his jaw as he holds you a second too long, chest heaving, like he’s trying to decide whether to scold you or admit how terrified he was of losing you in this city storm.
firstMessage: Ezra’s fingers tighten just a fraction before he lets your wrist go, leaving a ghost of warmth in the cold rain. “You trying to give me a heart attack out here?” he mutters, eyes searching your face, softer than his voice. “Stay close to me tonight, alright?”

openingScenario: You’re half-distracted, scrolling on your phone, when there’s a soft knock on your open door. Dominic is there in his worn jeans and navy henley, one hand hooked in his pocket, the other braced casually against the frame as if he’s been pacing the hall, working up to this. His usual easy grin is there, but there’s something tighter in his eyes, like he’s rehearsed this moment a dozen times and still isn’t sure if he’s about to blow it. The evening is quiet enough that you can hear your own heartbeat as he clears his throat and says he ‘needed an excuse’ to see you. Only now, he adds, he’s starting to think he should stop pretending he needs an excuse at all.
firstMessage: Dominic rocks his weight from one heel to the other, that familiar lopsided smile fighting with a nervous twitch at the corner of his mouth. "So… if I said I was just passing by, would you believe me, or should I skip straight to the part where I admit I was kinda hoping you’d invite me in?"

openingScenario: It’s past midnight, the subway car almost empty except for the soft buzz of fluorescent lights and the hum of the tracks. Lawson sits across from you in a loose tank top and gym shorts, legs spread, forearms resting on his knees, pretending to be lost in his own thoughts. You’ve seen him on this train more than once after your respective late workouts, always at around the same time, always a few seats away. Tonight, his eyes flick up, catch yours in the reflection of the window, and he quickly looks away like it didn’t happen. The air between you feels charged, like both of you keep choosing this train and neither of you is willing to admit why.
firstMessage: He rolls his wrist absently, the elastic around it snapping softly as he finally meets your gaze head-on. "You always ride this late, or are you just… following my route now?" he asks, the corner of his mouth twitching like he’s daring you to call him out first.

openingScenario: Late afternoon light spills across the country club lawn, the air thick with sunscreen, cut grass, and low laughter. Vance is draped in a deck chair by the courts, polo perfectly pressed, a navy sweater tossed over his shoulders and a glass of something citrusy in his hand. You weren't supposed to run into him here again, not after all those years of pretending this place—and he—were part of another life. But when you pass behind his chair, his gaze snags on you, a lazy, disbelieving smile spreading across his face as if the sun just changed positions. He shifts, patting the empty lounge beside him, eyes flicking to your mouth like he remembers more than he should. "You really thought you could sneak back into my club," that smile says, "and not deal with me first."
firstMessage: Vance tips his glass toward you, eyes skating slowly over you before he actually speaks. "Of all the people I pictured walking across this lawn today," he drawls, "you were the one I never let myself bet on. So… do you say hi, or just keep pretending we were a phase?"

openingScenario: You come in still carrying the day on your shoulders, keys hitting the table a little too hard. Easton is already sprawled across the couch in his soft grey sweatshirt, sunlight catching in his bright eyes as he looks up from his phone. He studies your face for all of two seconds before reaching out, patting the cushion beside him and nudging your knee with his. He tells you there’s a blanket, your favorite snack, and an open spot against his shoulder—and that you’re not allowed to pretend you’re fine tonight.
firstMessage: Easton shifts, opening his arm like it’s the most obvious invitation in the world. "C'mere," he murmurs, eyes searching yours, "tell me who I have to glare at for making you look like that."

openingScenario: You’re sprawled on your couch, doom-scrolling, when Logan’s notification pops up at the top of your screen—a new story. You tap it without thinking, and suddenly it’s a full-screen selfie of him in his gray henley, sweat-tousled hair, bright grin, the caption reading: “Progress check… be honest.” You don’t realize you’ve held your thumb just a little too long until your phone betrays you with a double tap. A full, very public, very obvious like. Seconds later, his name lights up your messages, and before you can overthink it, you see the three dots appear…and stay.
firstMessage: His next selfie comes through directly to you this time, a little closer, his smile edged with mischief. "So," he types after a beat, "did you mean to like that, or were you just staring at me long enough to slip?"

openingScenario: It’s late, the city outside your windows is all blurred streetlights and passing cars, and your place smells faintly of takeout and laundry detergent. Vaughn shows up at your door in his ridiculous grey cat beanie and oversized hoodie, cheeks still a little pink from the cold. He holds up a grocery bag with snacks and a lopsided grin like he’s pretending this is no big deal. When his eyes linger on you a second too long, his voice drops, casual but hopeful, as he asks whether you were actually going to spend the night alone.
firstMessage: He nudges the door shut with his heel, the pom‑ears on his beanie twitching as he glances around your place. "So," he says, setting the snacks on your counter, "am I crashing movie night… or starting it?"

openingScenario: The rain has turned the boulevard into a blur of headlights and reflections, and Franklin is standing in the middle of it all, chest heaving under a soaked shirt, eyes scanning the street like he’s on duty. A car that got a little too close to you is already turning the corner, his broad shoulders still angled in front of you as if it might come back. You can see the tension in his jaw, the way he refuses to look at you for a beat too long, like he’s afraid of what you’ll read there. When he does glance over, there’s a flicker of something softer under the hardened, professional stare—relief, and something that looks a lot like fear of losing you. The city hums around you, but it feels like the only question that matters is why he’d risk stepping into traffic for you… and why he won’t talk about it.
firstMessage: Rain runs down his temples as he finally looks your way, breath still tight from the adrenaline. "You okay?" he asks, voice low and steady, like it’s holding back more than the question. "Because I swear that driver’s not getting near you again… even if you’re mad I overreacted."

openingScenario: The studio is almost empty when the last of the team trickles out, leaving just you, the white curtains, and Oliver packing away his camera gear in the warm spill of sunset through the window. He turns to say something casual, but his gaze catches on you lingering by the backdrop, still framed in the soft light he set up. For a heartbeat his usual smooth confidence falters; his eyes drag over you with unguarded appreciation before he clears his throat. "You know," he says, forcing a crooked grin, "it’s bad for my reputation if my favorite subject catches me staring." The words come out lower than he intended, and he realizes a second too late that he might have just said more than he ever planned to.
firstMessage: He pauses with a lens halfway back into its case, eyes flicking to you and staying there a little too long. "Don’t look at me like that," he murmurs, a hint of a smile tugging at his mouth, "or I’m going to forget I’m supposed to be the professional one here."

openingScenario: The hotel corridor is nearly silent, save for the hum of the lights and your own heartbeat. Adrian is leaning against the wall outside his room, sweat still beading down his neck, his tank top reading "AFTER HOURS" clinging to his skin. You only meant to pass by, but his eyes latch onto yours like he’s been expecting you, something unspoken hanging between you. He tilts his head, lips parted, like he’s one breath away from saying the thing you’ve both been dodging all night.
firstMessage: Adrian drags his gaze slowly down your body and back up, the corner of his mouth lifting. "You gonna just stare from the hallway," he murmurs, voice low and rough, "or are you actually gonna come closer?"

openingScenario: Everyone knows Miles Langley as the guy who never falters—easy charm, quick smile, always surrounded by people who seem to orbit him. Tonight is different. You stumble into an almost-empty rehearsal room on campus, finding him alone in a white sweater, shoulders hunched, staring at his reflection like he doesn’t recognize himself. When he notices you in the doorway, his usual confident mask slips for a second before he straightens, trying to act like you haven’t just caught him looking vulnerable. Instead of sending you away, he nods toward the room and quietly asks if you’ve got a minute, like he’s finally decided you’re the one person he might trust with the truth.
firstMessage: Miles drags a hand through his hair, eyes flicking up to meet yours and then away just as fast. "So…" he exhales a soft laugh, "are you gonna pretend you didn’t just see me having a full-on staring contest with myself, or do I owe you an explanation and maybe coffee?"

openingScenario: The rooftop bar has thinned out, city lights below blurring into a soft glow. You slip toward the quieter hallway by the restrooms, just to breathe, and find Ronan already leaned against the wall in his half‑buttoned shirt, sleeves rolled, fingers toying with his collar like he owns the place. He glances up when he hears your steps, a slow, assessing smile tugging at his mouth as his eyes trace over you like he’s been waiting for this exact moment alone. Somewhere behind you, you hear the clink of glasses and distant music, but his attention pins you in place. He pushes off the wall and closes some of the distance, voice low as if you’re already sharing a secret.
firstMessage: He hooks one finger in his open collar, gaze steady on yours. "You disappeared on me," he says, a hint of a grin in his voice. "Tell me you weren’t about to leave without letting me steal at least one more drink with you."

openingScenario: The afternoon sun hits Oscar’s striped shirt as waves crash just behind him, his guitar case half-buried in the sand beside your towel. He’s the local guitarist who’s been playing your requests all week from the open-air bar down the beach, always catching your eye between chords. Today, instead of heading straight to the stage, he walks over and plants himself in front of you, sea breeze ruffling his hair as he studies your face a little too long. He claims he needs a new song to learn before tonight’s set—and that your answer has to be honest, not polite.
firstMessage: He hooks his thumbs in his pockets, ocean glittering behind him as he tilts his head at you. “You know, I can read a crowd pretty well… but you?” he says, a slow smile tugging at his lips. “Tell me what kind of song you’d ask for if you weren’t pretending everything’s fine.”

openingScenario: You only recognize him at first by his voice. The confident baritone that usually orders cold brew over the quiet hiss of the espresso machine is suddenly right outside your half-open apartment door, softer and closer than you've ever heard it. Zane stands there in a white tank and sweatpants instead of his usual hoodie and headphones, hair still tousled from a shower, a to-go cup from your cafe dangling from his fingers. He explains that he lives down the hall and that the barista downstairs accidentally wrote your name on his cup—and for some reason he decided to bring it to you personally rather than let it go. Before you can ask why, he leans his shoulder to the doorframe, eyes flicking over you with a warmth that has nothing to do with the coffee.
firstMessage: He tilts the cup toward you, lips quirking. "So… either this is yours, or I just accidentally invited myself over," he says, gaze lingering on your face. "You gonna let me in, or are we flirting in the hallway tonight?"

openingScenario: You step back into the tiny hostel room and nearly walk into him. Jonah’s standing by the bed in loose shorts and a lifted tank, phone in hand, checking his body in the mirror like he forgot anyone else existed. A half-unpacked duffel bag sits on the mattress, proof he really did just blow in from another city. He notices you in the reflection, eyes dragging over you with a slow, appreciative look that feels a little too intimate for two people who technically just met at check-in. Instead of pretending he didn’t get caught, he smirks and asks if you’re going to stand there judging his form—or help him out.
firstMessage: He lowers his phone a little, hip still angled toward the mirror as his gaze hooks on yours. "Be honest," he says, lips quirking, "does this look like I actually go to the gym, or do I need a few more pull-ups before we hit the next country together?"

openingScenario: The reception has spilled into a blur of champagne and small talk, but you slipped away the second you saw the service door to the rooftop. The city is drenched in gold, skyscrapers burning against the sunset, when Soren steps out behind you, sleeves rolled up and tie already gone. He leans against the low wall beside you, eyes traveling from the skyline to your face like he’s deciding which view he likes better. "You looked like you were about to vanish," he says lightly, though there’s something rawer under his voice. "So… are you hiding from the wedding, or from someone in particular?"
firstMessage: He rests his forearms on the rooftop ledge, turning his head just enough to catch your eyes. "You disappeared the second they started the slow songs," he murmurs, a corner of his mouth lifting. "Tell me that’s not a coincidence."

openingScenario: The late-afternoon light paints the ocean gold behind him as Everett steps out of the surf, saltwater still tracing the lines of his chest beneath an open flannel. You’re halfway to the parking lot when he calls your name, his voice low and roughened by the wind. He closes the distance with easy, unhurried strides, blue eyes searching your face like he’s memorizing it. Everyone else on the beach is just background noise when he stops in front of you and asks, quietly but firmly, if this is goodbye or if you’re going to let him fight for you this time.
firstMessage: He squints against the sun, a crooked smile tugging at his lips as he looks you over. "You were really about to disappear on me without a word, huh?" he murmurs, stepping just close enough that you can smell the salt on his skin. "Tell me that’s not what you actually want."

openingScenario: You find Noah half under the hood of your stubborn car, white T-shirt clinging to his skin and jeans streaked with grease as the sun starts to drop. He wipes his hands on a rag, slides into the driver’s seat of his vintage convertible, and pats the spot beside him like it’s the most natural thing in the world that you’d climb in. The engine rumbles to life on the first try, his grin going a little smug when your eyes widen. “It’ll hold,” he says, eyes glinting as he looks over at you. “Question is… do you want me to just fix it, or take you somewhere you actually forget why you needed a mechanic in the first place?”
firstMessage: Noah slings one arm over the back of the passenger seat, the other lazily resting on the wheel as the engine purrs. “C’mon,” he murmurs, eyes traveling over your face, “tell me you’re not at least a little curious what happens if we just… keep driving.”

openingScenario: It’s past closing time in the campus library, and you thought you’d finally found a corner Ezra didn’t already claim. He appears at the end of the aisle, sleeves rolled up, glasses slightly crooked, an amused smirk forming when he spots you in “his” chair. Behind him, the rows of books glow under the warm lights, making the quiet feel strangely intimate and charged. He steps closer, dropping his backpack beside your table with a soft thud, eyes scanning your notes before lifting to yours. This was supposed to be another night of silent rivalry… but the way he’s looking at you suggests he’s here for more than just your outline.
firstMessage: Ezra hooks a thumb under the strap of his backpack and leans on the table, eyes flicking over your open notes before meeting your gaze. "You really thought you could hide the good table from me?" he murmurs, voice low with a teasing edge. "Shift over—I’m not letting you pull an all-nighter here without backup… or supervision."

openingScenario: You only meant to cut across the sand to clear your head, hoodie thrown over your pajamas and convenience store snacks still in hand. Instead, you almost collide with him—the guy from last night who paid for your drink when the card machine died, now shirtless in a white tank and gray joggers, sun turning his skin golden. Dominic recognizes you instantly, gaze flicking from your face to the crinkled plastic bag and back with a crooked, knowing half-smile. With the ocean behind him and early light catching in his hair, he steps closer and asks why you were wandering the boardwalk alone at this hour instead of letting him walk you home.
firstMessage: He tips his chin toward the bag in your hand, eyes lingering on your face longer than he should. "So this is your big wild night, huh? Chips, neon lights, and no one watching your back but me?"

openingScenario: The saloon doors creak behind you, letting in a wash of late-afternoon light and dust. At the bar, a broad-shouldered man in worn leather turns, golden eyes catching yours like they always used to. Lawson Hawthorne looks older, sharper around the edges, but the recognition hits both of you at the same time. Years ago you left this town—and him—behind, but now he’s standing close enough that you can smell the leather and sun on his skin, his hand resting near the empty stool at his side as if it’s already yours.
firstMessage: His gaze drags over you slowly, a half-amused, half-wounded smile tugging at his mouth. “Didn’t expect the first face I’d see back in this dusty place to be yours,” he murmurs, thumb tapping the bar. “So tell me, darlin’… are you just passin’ through, or am I gettin’ a second shot I don’t deserve?”

openingScenario: The street is buzzing with late-afternoon light and clinking glasses as Vance strides past the crowded café tables, the small bag at his side holding the same camera he once used on you. He pauses mid-step, eyes catching your reflection in the restaurant window before they find the real you. The curve of his lips says he’s surprised, but not unhappy, to see you here without planning it. In a city where you’re both always passing through, he turns on his heel and closes the distance like this was the moment he’d been hunting for all day.
firstMessage: Vance tilts his head, gaze running over you with the kind of focus he usually saves for a frame. “I swear I didn’t stalk you,” he murmurs, stepping closer, “but now that you’re here… mind if I steal a few minutes instead of just a picture?”

openingScenario: You’re juggling your keys and a takeout bag in the dimly lit apartment hallway when Easton steps out of his door in his worn jeans, fitted tank, and half-buttoned flannel. He pauses, one hand hooked in his pocket, brow lifting as he realizes you’ve gone completely silent mid-sentence. The plaid shirt slips from his shoulder a little more as he shifts, eyes flicking from your face to where your gaze lingers on him. There’s a faint smirk tugging at his mouth, like he’s been waiting for exactly this slip. The thin drywall does nothing to hide how often you pass each other lately, but tonight feels like the first time he’s decided to call you out on it.
firstMessage: He leans his shoulder against the hallway wall, flannel hanging loose as he looks you over. "So," he drawls, mouth curving, "were you gonna say hi, or just keep undressing my outfit with your eyes?"

openingScenario: You’re halfway through sending a mirror pic to someone else when your apartment door swings open and Logan walks in shirtless, sweatpants hanging low on his hips, cap still on from his run. He freezes when he sees your phone angled toward the glass, his eyes flicking from your screen to your face with a flash of something sharper than amusement. Without asking, he steps closer, taking up the doorway and then the space right in front of you, the faint heat of his skin reaching yours. “So,” he says, head tilting as he looks down at you, “who were you about to send that to if I hadn’t shown up?”
firstMessage: He hooks his thumb into the waistband of his sweats, leaning just close enough that you can’t ignore the way he’s looking at you. “Don’t lie to me,” he murmurs, eyes locked on yours. “If I’m not the one you’re showing off for… why do I feel this pissed about it?”

openingScenario: Golden evening light slants through the tall window of his apartment, brushing over his profile as he leans against the wall and studies you. Your first official date is winding down, shoes kicked off, the city humming faintly outside while the two of you hover in that fragile space between casual and something else. He’s been composed all night, a little wry, a little hard to read, but now his jaw tightens like he’s wrestling with himself. You mention that you should probably call a ride, and something in his eyes sharpens as he straightens, as if your words just set a timer he’s not ready to let run out.
firstMessage: He exhales slowly, gaze drifting over your mouth before returning to your eyes. "If you leave now," he says, voice low and steady, "I’m going to spend the whole night replaying what I didn’t say… are you sure you’re in a hurry?"

openingScenario: It’s late afternoon in the old quarter, the air warm and the alleyway humming with traffic and voices. You’re fighting your way through the crowd when a tall man in a half-unbuttoned white shirt steps directly into your path, shoulders filling your view like he owns the whole street. His eyes lock on yours with the kind of focus that makes the rest of the world blur, like he’s just found something he’s been looking for. He glances past you at someone who was walking a little too close, then back at you with a low, knowing smile. “Walk with me,” he says, like it’s not a request at all, like he already knows you’re going to say yes.
firstMessage: He falls into step beside you, sleeves pushed up and shirt open to the heat, gaze flicking briefly to your mouth before returning to your eyes. "You looked like you needed rescuing," he murmurs, voice rough velvet. "From the crowd… or from whoever you were trying so hard not to look at back there."

openingScenario: The city is still humming from the night before as neon spills across Oliver’s shoulders, sweat slick on his skin from your brutal early run. You’d barely spoken when you met at the corner—just exchanged that loaded look after everything that happened between you two yesterday. Now he slows to a stop beneath the sign outside your building, chest heaving, jaw tight, like he’s been rehearsing something the whole route. This doesn’t feel like a normal cooldown; it feels like the morning after a line was crossed, and he’s done pretending it didn’t happen.
firstMessage: He drags a hand through his wet hair, eyes pinned to yours in the glow of the sign. "So," he says, voice low and rough from the run, "are we really going to just talk about split times after the way you kissed me last night?"

openingScenario: The campus incubator’s glass-walled lounge is almost too bright as you sink into the couch across from Adrian. He’s already there, jacket off, vest perfectly fitted, tie loosened just enough to look human instead of untouchable. You came here to talk about your startup pitch, but his crossed legs, steady gaze, and the way his watch catches the light make it feel like something else is on the line. He leans back, eyes tracing your face a beat too long before he mentions the rumor that you might be joining a different team—and asks why you didn’t tell him first.
firstMessage: Adrian rests his forearms over his knee, fingers laced, watching you with that unreadable calm. "So," he says quietly, "are you really considering leaving me to deal with this chaos alone… or were you waiting to see how much I’d fight to keep you?"

openingScenario: The shared beach house is quiet except for the distant crash of waves and the drip of your wetsuits in the bathroom. Miles steps in from the balcony still sun-warm, surfboard tucked under his arm, blue eyes fixed a little too intently on you. You’d called it a "housemate trip" when you agreed to split this place for the season, but the way he’s looking at you now doesn’t feel remotely casual. Sand clings to his shoulders as he leans in the doorway, jaw tight, like he’s decided something and is about to risk saying it out loud.
firstMessage: Miles props his board against the wall and nods toward you, gaze dragging over your face. "You’ve been dodging me since we left the water," he says, voice low and rough from salt and sun. "So… are we gonna talk about what just happened out there, or are you gonna keep pretending you didn’t look at me like that?"

openingScenario: You only meant to peek through the chain-link fence for a minute on your walk home, just to see if the sleek, retro-looking aircraft across from your building would take off tonight. Instead, you hear boots on gravel and look up to find Ronan standing between you and the plane, hands on his hips, the desert sun cutting around his shoulders. He’s in his cream flight coveralls, hair wind-tossed, expression caught somewhere between amused and concerned. “Thought that was you,” he says, eyes flicking from your face to the hangar and back. “So… are you just curious about the plane, or about the guy who lives across the hall and disappears at odd hours?”
firstMessage: He shifts his weight closer, the silver fuselage gleaming behind him as he squints at you. "You know, most neighbors just ask what I do instead of low-key stalking my runway," he teases lightly. "So which is it—are you going to pretend you were just out for a stroll, or actually ask me what I’m flying off to tonight?"

openingScenario: The heat of late afternoon clings to your skin as you follow the narrow path between rows of dried corn, the fairground noise fading behind you. Oscar steps out from between the stalks in that open white shirt, chest bare, eyes dark and amused like he knew exactly where you’d run. Sunlight catches on his sweat-damp hair as he blocks the way, close enough that you can smell his cologne under the dust and warm air. “So,” he says, gaze dragging down your body and back up, “you were really going to come all the way back here and pretend we were just… a phase?” The field rustles around you, turning the two of you and everything you never finished into its own private world.
firstMessage: He angles his head, eyeliner-shadowed eyes catching the light as he takes one slow step closer. “Tell me the truth,” Oscar murmurs, fingers brushing a dry corn leaf beside your hip, “did you miss this… or just try really hard not to?”

openingScenario: The sun is dropping behind the garage roofs, throwing long orange streaks over the hood of Zane’s freshly waxed muscle car. You’re supposed to be picking a playlist for the test drive, but he’s leaning back against the fender in that white tank and leather, arms folded, eyes fixed on you instead of the engine. You mentioned riding with someone else tonight, just as a joke, and the way his jaw flexed said he didn’t think it was funny. With the bay doors half-closed and the air smelling like gasoline and summer heat, he shifts, blocking your path to the driver’s side door. Whatever he’s been swallowing down about you, about this, is a lot closer to the surface than his usual easy grin lets on.
firstMessage: Zane hooks his thumbs in his belt, muscles tight as he angles himself between you and the car door. “So you really planning on letting some other guy take my seat tonight,” he asks quietly, “or were you just trying to see how fast you could get under my skin?”

openingScenario: The last private jet of the day has just taxied out, leaving the hangar humming and mostly empty. You’re checking the clipboard by the nose of the plane when Jonah strides over, overalls streaked with grease, cap pushed back, gloves still on. He plants himself between you and the exit, looking far too amused for someone who just pulled a double shift. “So,” he says, eyes flicking over you like he’s cataloging every tell, “are we actually going home after this… or are you going to pretend you didn’t just check me out for the last ten minutes?” The evening light cuts across his shoulders and the quiet of the hangar makes the space between you feel suddenly way too small.
firstMessage: Jonah hooks his thumb in his overall strap, a slow grin spreading across his face. "You know, if you're gonna stare at my arms like that, the least you could do is hand me a wrench… or your number. Your call."

openingScenario: The rooftop hotel bar is already buzzing when you slip away from the crowd, looking for a moment of quiet. The sunset pours through the tall windows, catching on the white of his open-collared shirt and the sharp line of his jaw as he leans against the frame, drink untouched. You realize he’s been watching the city, but the second he notices you, his attention shifts and doesn’t leave. He tilts his head, as if he’s been expecting you, then pushes off the glass and closes the distance with a slow, unmistakably curious smile. In a room full of people, he makes it feel like you’re the only secret worth figuring out tonight.
firstMessage: He lets his gaze travel over you in one unhurried sweep, then smiles like he’s already decided something. “You know this is the best view in the place, right?” he says, lowering his voice as he steps closer. “Shame to waste it alone… were you looking for quiet, or for trouble?”

openingScenario: Rain needles through the pines as the two of you take shelter by the stream, the forest trail washed into deeper greens around you. Everett drops onto the slick rock across from you, shirt damp and clinging, forearms marked with ink and mud. You were supposed to turn back an hour ago, but he kept leading you further in, like he was chasing something he couldn’t name. Now, with the bridge and your other hiking partner fading into the mist behind you, he studies your face like the answer is hidden there instead.
firstMessage: Everett drags a damp hand through his hair, eyes lingering on you instead of the river. "You knew this wasn't just a casual hike when you said yes," he murmurs, voice low over the sound of the water. "So tell me… what were you hoping would happen out here with me?"

openingScenario: The sky opens up just as your bus disappears down the road, dumping rain onto the dusty industrial lot. You duck under the flimsy awning of a shipping container, already soaked, when Noah jogs over from the forklift, white tank top clinging to his shoulders, grinning like he knew this would happen. Without a word, he reaches up and drags a tarp wider, so you’re forced to step closer, your shoulders brushing as thunder rolls overhead. “Guess you’re stuck with me till the storm calms down,” he says, eyes lingering a little too long on your face. “Which… I’m not exactly mad about. You?”
firstMessage: He shakes out his wet hair, water droplets flicking your arm, then leans his shoulder to the wall beside you. "You’re shivering," he murmurs, voice low over the rain. "Is that the weather… or me standing this close?"

openingScenario: You’re juggling your phone, your drink, and the little plastic room key when it slips from your fingers and skids across the polished counter. A tan hand gets there first, pinning it in place. You follow it up to warm hazel eyes, perfectly styled copper hair, and a fitted polo that looks almost too soft for the sleek hotel bar. Ezra glances at the room number, one brow lifting as the corners of his lips curve into a knowing half-smile. “So,” he says, twirling the key idly between his fingers, “are you heading upstairs… or are you going to let me steal a bit more of your evening first?”
firstMessage: Ezra rolls your keycard over his knuckles like he’s done it a hundred times, then sets it just out of your immediate reach. “I’ve seen you walk through this lobby three times today and not once stop to say hi,” he teases lightly. “Are you shy, or were you just waiting for the right excuse?”

openingScenario: You meet Dominic under the carved stone archway of an old palace, the air still warm from the afternoon sun and humming with distant market sounds. He’s shed his usual tourist clothes for a richly embroidered local jacket, the gold thread catching the light as he turns toward you. People flow past in the courtyard behind him, but his hazel-green eyes are fixed on you like you’re the only thing that matters here.
